# Summary of Cairn Mechanics

## Core Concepts

A cairn is a height value that can grow, shrink, or be combined with other cairns through various mechanical operations. The mechanics are all deterministic—given the same starting conditions and operations, you always get the same result.

## Pulse (Growth)

A pulse makes a cairn taller based on its current size. The boost isn't fixed; it scales with height:
1. Divide current height by stride value (floor division)
2. Add the stride value to that quotient to get the boost amount
3. Add the boost to current height

The key insight: taller cairns get bigger boosts, so growth accelerates over successive pulses.

## Leak (Post-Pulse Loss)

After a pulse, a leak removes marks proportional to the new height:
1. Divide the post-pulse height by the leak value (floor division)
2. Subtract that amount from the height

A leak always happens after a pulse in the same cycle.

## Drain (Sustained Loss)

A drain is a repeating cycle of pulse followed by a fixed loss. Unlike a leak (proportional), a drain removes the same number of marks every cycle. As the cairn shrinks, the pulse boost shrinks too, eventually making the boost too weak to overcome the drain loss. The cairn reaches zero at some point.

## Pulse-Leak Cycles

You can repeat pulse-leak cycles multiple times, applying the new height as the starting point for the next cycle. Recalculate everything fresh each time—don't reuse old numbers.

## Finding Origins

Given an end result, you work backwards by testing candidate starting heights and running them forward through the same operations to see which one matches the target.

## Merging

Two cairns combine into one using a weighted average formula:
1. Floor-divide each height by 10
2. Multiply each floored value by its weight (as a fraction out of 10)
3. Add the weighted values
4. Apply a tether adjustment (fixed value, can be positive or negative)
5. Apply a scaling adjustment based on the difference between the two floored values (exact formula unclear but relates to their relationship)
